title: The Sick Lion and the Fox
text:
A lion had grown old and weak and could no longer hunt by strength. So he decided to hunt by cunning. He went into his cave, lay down, and let it be known throughout the forest that he was very ill.

The other animals felt sorry for him. One after another they came to the cave to pay their respects and ask how he was. Each one went in, and the lion, lying in wait in the dark, seized and ate it. In this way he fed well without ever having to leave his den.

After many animals had gone missing, the fox came by. He did not go in. He stood outside the entrance, at a respectful distance, and politely asked the king how he was feeling.

The lion answered that he was very poorly and invited the fox to step inside so they could talk more comfortably. The fox thanked him but declined. He had noticed, he said, a great many footprints leading into the cave, and not a single one coming out. Then he went on his way.
lesson: Before you accept an invitation, look at the evidence of what happened to those who accepted before you. The track record says more than the host.
